title: 57th GMA Dove Awards: Complete Winners List Revealed – Gospel Music Association Highlights 2024 Victors
body:
The 57th GMA Dove Awards celebrated a night of soaring performances and surprise triumphs, with worship veterans and breakout artists alike sharing the spotlight. Phil Wickham, Brandon Lake, Josiah Queen, Jamie MacDonald, Tasha Cobbs Leonard and gospel legend CeCe Winans each walked away with top honors, underscoring a year that blended traditional hymnody with fresh, genre‑bending sounds. The ceremony, which aired in an encore broadcast on Friday, Oct. 16, highlighted the evolving landscape of Christian music while reaffirming the genre’s deep‑rooted commitment to ministry and community.

The evening opened with a rousing rendition of “Living Hope,” performed by a choir of past Dove winners, setting a tone of reverence and celebration. Phil Wickham, who clinched Artist of the Year and Song of the Year for his anthemic “Hymn of Heaven,” thanked fans for “making the sky feel like home.” His win marks the second time he has topped the Dove Awards, cementing his status as a bridge between contemporary worship and classic hymn structures. Across the stage, Brandon Lake, fresh off a chart‑topping collaboration with Elevation Worship, secured New Artist of the Year, a nod to his rapid ascent from church‑plant worship leader to mainstream Christian radio staple.

Josiah Queen’s victory in the Rap/Hip‑Hop Recorded Song category signaled the genre’s growing influence within the Christian music sphere. His track “Grace on the Run” blended trap beats with scripture‑laden verses, earning praise for lyrical depth and cultural relevance. Meanwhile, Jamie MacDonald’s win for Inspirational Album of the Year with “Grace & Glory” reflected a resurgence of acoustic‑driven worship that appeals to both older congregants and younger listeners seeking intimacy in worship. The diversity of winners illustrates the Dove Awards’ expanding definition of what constitutes gospel and worship music today.

Veteran gospel powerhouse Tasha Cobbs Leonard captured Female Vocalist of the Year, a testament to her sustained impact after a near‑decade hiatus. Her powerful delivery on “Your Spirit” resonated with audiences yearning for soulful, prayerful expression. CeCe Winans, a perennial favorite, added another accolade to her storied career by winning Contemporary Gospel/Urban Recorded Song of the Year for “Believe for It.” Her win not only highlights her enduring relevance but also underscores the seamless blend of gospel tradition with contemporary production that has become a hallmark of modern Christian music.

Industry insiders note that this year’s awards reflected a strategic shift toward inclusivity and cross‑genre collaborations. The presence of artists like Aaron Cole, whose folk‑inflected “Heart of the World” earned Songwriter of the Year, and the surprise nomination of a virtual‑reality worship collective, points to a broader embrace of innovative worship expressions. Record labels have responded by investing in hybrid projects that marry worship choruses with EDM, hip‑hop, and even Latin rhythms, aiming to reach a global, digitally native audience.

Looking ahead, the momentum generated by the 57th Dove Awards suggests a continued blurring of lines between worship, gospel, and mainstream Christian music. As streaming platforms amplify niche subgenres and churches adopt more eclectic worship sets, artists are likely to experiment further, pushing theological themes into new sonic territories. The upcoming 58th GMA Dove Awards, slated for next spring, will undoubtedly showcase how today’s trailblazers influence the next wave of faith‑based artistry, keeping the genre both rooted in tradition and forward‑looking.
